article:
Money makes it a product

A payment is not a badge. It is the moment a stranger trusts you with a card. Stripe is the default in this house: a test mode that uses fake cards, a live mode that uses real ones, and webhooks — Stripe knocking on your door to say the money actually moved.

Until a webhook has told you “paid,” you do not unlock the thing. A thank-you page is not proof. People close tabs. Networks lie. Stripe does not.

The first pound

Test cards first. Then one real pound, to yourself, on live keys, on a product that can also refund you. That pound teaches more than a course. After that you can talk about prices.

Do not invent a billing system. Prices change. Seats change. Stripe already did the miserable part.

How I actually do it

Billboard is a price that only goes up — that is a payments story I am not telling in public until the following exists. Send Reorder has to charge shops. Inner circle on this site, when it exists, is a Stripe checkout and a door, not a PDF.

I keep live keys in env, never in the repo. I keep test and live straight in my head. Mixing them is how you “succeed” with a card that was never real.

Where noobs get stuck

Building a whole shop before a £1 button. Or going live with test keys. Or trusting the redirect and never handling the webhook. Or being so shy about charging that the product stays a favour forever.

Film this

Stripe test mode. The fake card number. The webhook arriving. Then — if you are willing — one live pound and a refund. Silence after the refund is the end card.

Do this before chapter 13

  • Make a Stripe account. Stay in test mode.
  • Put a £1 button on a page. Pay with a test card.
  • Log the webhook. Read it. Do not ignore it.
  • Write the sentence you will charge for. If you cannot, you are not ready to charge.

Next: email — the app wrote to the user. DNS again.
